newsitem.title: UK: ONS says cheaper meat cuts UK output prices.
newsitem.headline: ONS says cheaper meat cuts UK output prices.

text.p: The Office for National Statistics (ONS) said UK February output prices were depressed by lower meat prices, particularly pig meat because of competition from imports.

The annual rise in ouput prices for food products and beverages was just 0.2 percent, the lowest since before 1975 when the series began. By comparison, food products and beverage prices increased by an annual rate of 1.1 percent in January.

The ONS added that lower petrol prices, because of a fall in crude oil prices, had also depressed the overall output prices index. It said the output price of petrol products fell by 1.3 percent between February and January.
The ONS said that lower unadjusted input prices partially reflected cheaper winter tariffs for electricity and there would also be an impact on March data.
Fuel prices fell by 3.1 percent between February and January. Electricity represents around two-thirds of the fuel component.

It added unadjusted output prices excluding excise duties rose by an annual 0.6 percent in February, the lowest rate of increase since September 1986 when there was a rise of 0.4 percent. In January, by contrast, the rise in ouput prices excluding excise duties was 1.0 percent.
The series excludes excise duties payable on tobacco products, alcoholic liquor and petroleum products.
